report.summary: Wiki layer (links.py build_index) and structcore index (via markdown.knowledge_links) both resolve wikilinks to edges using candidate logic (path-first, then title, ambiguous dropped). Duplication is indicated by comments: index.py mentions 'markdown.py parses [[wikilinks]] and resolves doc->doc and doc->code'. Not fully visible in slice, but high risk of drift. Resolution ownership should be unified.
risks: Link resolution rules (e.g., _candidates_for in links.py) may diverge between wiki and index, causing inconsistent edge sets for the same content.
If resolution logic is duplicated, a bug fix in one place may be missed in the other, leading to incorrect links in diagnostic outputs (local graph vs. document_links).
The index's wiki gate (DAEDALUS_INDEX_WIKI) suggests a separate code path that may not fully replicate links.py's deterministic sort, bounds, and edge types.
todos: Locate markdown.knowledge_links or equivalent in structcore/markdown.py and compare with wiki/links.py build_index.
Decide which component owns resolutio: preferably wiki layer exports a reusable LinkIndex builder, and index.py calls it when documents+wiki flags are on.
Verify that type: and vault: link handling is consistent across both; currently links.py just counts them, but index may attempt resolution.
Check that ambiguous/unresolved reporting is uniform; links.py reports, but index's document_links may silently drop.

handoff.suggestion: Refactor: have structcore/index.py import and use wiki.links.build_index directly, to avoid duplicated candidate resolution. Remove the internal markdown link resolution for wikilinks, keeping only pure markdown []() links separate. This ensures one source of truth for [[wikilink]] semantics.
